Despite a BNP result of over 4000 and a hospital echocardiogram showing serious cardiac issues, no one from the surgery contacted us to explain the findings or arrange any follow-up.

When we saw Dr Steve Allen to discuss the results, he told us “GPs don’t go through echocardiograms,” refused to explain the report, offered no reassurance, and didn’t carry out any observations or medication review. The consultation lasted 7 minutes and left my grandmother upset and humiliated.

We only received an urgent referral because I personally chased the hospital directly — the GP hadn’t sent one, despite knowing the result. It was only after a hospital manager intervened that the referral was finally made.

Dr Allen routinely declines phone consultations and instead sends vague, grammatically poor one-line text messages, even for serious clinical findings. One example was when a chest X-ray revealed fluid on my grandmother’s lungs — he sent a single text instead of calling or reviewing her in person. This kind of communication is completely inappropriate and shows a lack of care or urgency.
